Liam — appreciate the specificity. A few quick items based on our standard playbook: 

- We can accommodate a temporary downward adjustment on material usage contraction, provided the adjustment is: (a) time-boxed (max 6 months), (b) subject to a documented reconciliation, and (c) not below the Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) for the contract term.
- We cannot accept an unbounded "market adjustment" clause; any market repricing needs to be tied to an objective index or a mutually agreed reprice table at renewal.
- For termination-triggered adjustments, suggest renaming the clause to "Termination True-up and Transitional Pricing" and define a 90-day reconciliation window following termination to agree final usage and any credit/true-up.

Suggested compromise in advance of the call: accept a 6-month temporary repricing limited to the difference between invoiced charges and the MMC (i.e., customer cannot reduce billings to below MMC) and institute a smoothing mechanism where the full adjustment phases in over up to 4 billing periods. If BlueWave insists on a lower absolute floor than MMC, we would require a minimum guarantee or a one-time non-refundable ramp credit.

I'll prepare a clean counter-redline this morning and send to the thread.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

4) Carve out promotional/trial usage from the calculation to avoid triggering on ramp-down after pilots.
